To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
eye movements are a reflection of cognitive processing.

(1) eye movements in reading are controlled by the cognitive system, (2) the cognitive processes involved in reading can be described in terms of a parallel, interactive, and cascading architecture, (3) the cognitive processes in reading can be characterized in terms of the perceptual span (the region of text that is processed during a fixation), and (4) the cognitive processes are influenced by the nature of the material to be read and the task requirements.
(a) eye movements reflect cognitive processes, (b) cognitive processes can be studied by examining eye movements, and (c) eye movements are useful for understanding cognitive processes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cognitive processing of information in the human brain.
the cognitive processes that underlie eye movements and the role of eye movement data in understanding those processes.
how people process information in various situations, and eye movements provide a unique and powerful window into these processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of eye movements in information processing tasks is a valuable and productive research tool.
eye movement research is a powerful tool that can be used to study cognitive processes.
eye movements are useful for understanding cognitive processes in general, and reading in particular, and for understanding individual differences in these processes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
eye movements are the best measure we have of moment-to-moment cognitive processes.
reading is a highly skilled, automatic, and efficient process that is characterized by the use of the foveal, parafoveal, and peripheral vision in a highly organized manner.
the use of eye movements to study reading and other information-processing tasks has been fruitful, and that the future use of eye movement techniques will be equally fruitful.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the study of eye movements in information processing provides a unique window into the cognitive processes involved in the task.
eye movement studies can be used to examine the cognitive processes involved in various information processing tasks.
eye movements provide a window into cognitive processing that is not available in any other way.
